# Cherie (01, engineer) — SPD-087

## Brief
Close Law 7's git verb table so no name git answers to writes the repository for a spudagent unseen.

The defect. `git_refused` (bin/spudlib/shell/git_verbs.py) refuses a member the fixed set `syntax.GIT_WRITE_VERBS`, plus the subcommand-aware cases (stash, worktree, remote, reflog, branch, tag, config). git dispatches several of its own commands to the same code under another name, and its plumbing writes the index, the object database and the working tree under names the set does not hold. Probed on git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157), SPD-049: `git stage -h` prints "usage: git add [<options>] [--] <pathspec>..." and `git init-db -h` prints "usage: git init [-q | --quiet] [--bare] ..."; neither is in the set, so `git_refused` returns None and the hook is silent for a member. `git checkout-index -a --prefix=<dir>/` wrote the entire tree into a scratch directory, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<f> git read-tree HEAD` wrote a 44 KB index. The ticket also names read-tree, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree, hash-object -w, merge-file, repack, pack-refs, fast-import, unpack-objects, index-pack, sparse-checkout, maintenance, fsck-objects, replay, merge-index, merge-one-file, merge-ours, merge-recursive*, merge-subtree, subtree, send-pack, receive-pack and update-server-info.

Do not stop at the ticket's list. `git --list-cmds=main` on this Mac holds about 170 names, and the ticket's list is a sample of one reading. Names it does not mention, each worth a probe of its own: backfill, quiltimport, imap-send, http-push, http-fetch, fetch-pack, bundle, mktag, mktree, prune-packed, pack-objects, rerere, refs (`git refs migrate` rewrites the ref storage), hook (`git hook run <name>` runs the repository's own hook script), p4, daemon, http-backend, shell, upload-pack, upload-archive, submodule--helper, checkout--worker, difftool--helper, fsmonitor--daemon, credential-store, credential-cache, remote-ext and remote-fd (the URL names a command git runs). Sweep every name the list gives, decide read or write for each with evidence, and say in the module comment how you decided.

Decide the shape first, and record the decision with its reasons in your Result. Two candidates: (a) extend GIT_WRITE_VERBS, the denylist SPD-044 and SPD-049 built on, keeping the existing per-verb subcommand cases; (b) invert to an allowlist of git's read-only verbs, refusing a member every other name, which fails closed on a git version that adds a writer. The hook already fails closed on a verb absent from `git --list-cmds=main` (tests/test_hooks.py::test_the_command_list_is_read_from_git_and_fails_closed), so (b) is continuous with what is there; it is also the larger change, and it must not start refusing a member the read verbs it needs. Whichever you pick, a verb that only reads must stay silent and a verb that writes must be refused with Law 7's own reason.

## Ticket proposals
- **A member's format-patch, bugreport and diagnose write a file into the working directory no rule sees** — suggested P2; open, with Spud.
  Why: SPD-049 lets a member run these verbs and checks the path they name; each also has a default form that names no path at all and writes into the current directory, which neither Law 7's verb reading nor the path rule sees. SPD-087 left them allowed because their writing forms are SPD-049's and overturning that division is another ticket's call, but the gap is real: a member can drop files into a checkout outside its deliverables with no refusal. The fix is probably a third small table -- the verbs whose default writing form the line never spells -- read like GIT_VERB_FILE_POSITIONALS but with the cwd as the target.
  Evidence: Probed on git 2.54.0 (Apple Git-157): 'git format-patch -1' writes 0001-<subject>.patch into the current directory ('git format-patch -h': [<options>] [<since> | <revision-range>], with -o/--output-directory optional); 'git bugreport' writes git-bugreport-<date>.txt and 'git diagnose' a zip into the current directory when -o is absent (both usage lines make -o optional). tests/test_hooks.py::GitFileWriteTest asserts the silence today: self.assertSilent('git format-patch -1') and 'git bugreport -o tests/out'. git archive and git mailsplit have no such form (archive writes stdout with no -o, mailsplit requires -o).
